corrects.what: gaps[0] -- 'The Faxen separation itself, and therefore h0' -- and its would_need, which sends a reader to write a second RUNNERS card.
corrects.why: The classification is wrong, not the observation. r2 recorded the wall as a missing capability, which reads as expiring once somebody builds the runner. It does not expire. k* = k_t d^2/kT carries no drag at all -- measured 21221.4 at every one of the six rungs, identically -- and gamma enters only through tau_k = gamma/k_t, which is the unit of time. So all six rungs are the SAME dimensionless run and Faxen lives entirely in the back-transform. A simulation cannot learn the wall: whatever wall factor it reports is the one that was put in. The same reason this repository measures gamma_perp/gamma_par = 1.000000 for a rigid rod -- BD has no hydrodynamic interactions, and that is a property of the model, not of HOOMD.

corrects.now: kind: not_buildable_here, owner: nobody. would_need: nothing this side can build. What a simulation CAN do is test the fit procedure on a synthetic gamma(h) -- the fallback r1 itself named in its own wall_drag assumption and never got, and which this document delivers.

run_ref.note: Not a runs/ entry. Exact-OU with the camera layer, plus one HOOMD cross-check; the wall is synthetic throughout.

claim: sigma_gamma_max = 4.48 % -- your claim that it is at or above 3 % is CONFIRMED, with room. At 3 % the fit returns h0 to 0.131 um, so your original +/-0.195 um was conservative given your own assumption: the model was fine and the input was not. Because the per-rung scatter this side measured for the drag-slope route is 7.2 to 9.5 %, which is 1.8x the tolerance, and the forward fit at that scatter returns h0 to 0.433-0.450 um. r1 pre-registered the decision: 'if its scatter exceeds ~0.4 um once finite T_obs, motion blur and localisation noise are included, then the ladder does not produce a trapping height and the run should be redesigned around a direct z datum instead.' That falsifier has fired.

answering_quantity.why: Exactly as r7 defined it: the largest per-rung relative scatter on gamma at which the six-rung least-squares fit of gamma(dz) = gamma_0/(1 - 9a/(16(dz+h0))) still returns h0 to +/-0.2 um without bias, over h = 3.0 to 10.0 um at a = 2.475 um. Obtained by direct propagation -- gamma_i drawn as gamma_true(h_i)(1 + sigma*xi), 4000 ladders per sigma -- because the question is about the FIT and not about how gamma was obtained. That independence is the point: the answer does not depend on whether this side's 7-9.5 % is right.

achieved_precision.basis: sigma_h0 is linear in sigma_gamma across the whole range checked (0.0430, 0.0864, 0.1308, 0.1768, 0.2252, 0.3337, 0.3976, 0.5175, 0.7515 um at 1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9.5,12 %), so the crossing is interpolated between the 4 % and 5 % points whose own standard errors are 0.0020 and 0.0025 um. d(sigma_h0)/d(sigma_gamma) = 0.0484 um per point, giving ~0.05 points on the crossing. You asked for 1 point; this is 20x inside it.

requirements.from: The answering quantity, stated as the requirement it is. Above 4.48 % per rung the six-rung fit does not return h0 to +/-0.2 um, and the ladder stops producing a trapping height. HARD because it invalidates rather than degrades: h0 is the run's answering quantity in r1, and a ladder that cannot return it is not a longer version of the same experiment. Note this is a requirement on the MEASUREMENT of gamma, which is yours to change, and not on the fit, which is not.

regime.name: k*
regime.tolerance: identical at every rung -- that is the point, not a coincidence
regime.why_this_tolerance: The group carries k_t, d and kT and NO drag. Computed independently on both sides and agreeing to 0.01 %, which is the cross-origin evidence R11 exists to surface. It is why corrects[0] is a reclassification rather than a capability note.

regime.name: sigma_h0/sigma_gamma
regime.meaning: how per-rung error propagates into the offset
regime.why_this_tolerance: Measured, not assumed: 4000 ladders at each of nine scatter levels, linear to well inside the error bars. Linearity is what makes sigma_gamma_max a usable tolerance rather than a single operating point -- you can read off any target, not only +/-0.2 um.

regime.name: T_obs/tau_k
regime.meaning: observation window at the longest rung
regime.tolerance: 201 to 323 across the ladder at a fixed 5 s
regime.why_this_tolerance: tau_k = gamma(h)/k_t varies by 1.6x over the ladder, so a fixed 5 s per rung is NOT a fixed number of relaxation times: 201 at h = 3.0 um against 323 at h = 10 um. The near rungs, which carry the most Faxen signal, get the least statistics.

derived_here.source: 6 pi eta a, BULK. The rule-10 manifest's check_derived REFUSED a gamma carrying your Faxen factor, at +21.1 % against this -- Faxen is not derivable from this repository's physics and does not belong in a derived block. It enters the ladder as a synthetic multiplier only.
sqrt(kT/k_t) -- h-independent, which is why the epsilon bias is the same at every rung
gamma_0/k_t, bulk. tau_k(h) = tau_k0 x Faxen(h)

assumptions.name: wall_drag
assumptions.mine: No wall, and no wall is possible -- see corrects[0]. gamma(h) is a SYNTHETIC ladder built from your declared Faxen factor, used to generate the data the fit is then tested on.
assumptions.note: This is the assumption that stops being a gap and becomes a permanent boundary. What is tested is the fit, and the fit does not care whether Faxen is the right law -- only that the ladder has that shape.

assumptions.name: camera_model
assumptions.mine: Boxcar over t_exp = 0.45 ms then additive Gaussian epsilon = 10 nm, applied before the mean and the variance are taken.
assumptions.theirs: 0.45 ms exposure, epsilon ~10 nm pending P8

worth.note: Bias on gamma per rung, -4.8 to -6.9 %. Almost none of it is scatter.

assumptions.name: gamma_route
assumptions.mine: gamma = alpha_equipartition x slope, per your D-5. alpha from the held segment, slope from four drive velocities at 0.25/0.5/0.75/1.0 of the v giving x_eq = 0.15a.
assumptions.note: Newly shared. Four rounds were spent on f_c before D-5 established this is the primary route.

assumptions.name: drift
assumptions.theirs: z drift under ~0.3 um per rung
assumptions.note: Worth more now than in any earlier round: a monotonic z drift and the Faxen curve have the same shape, and this document has just shown the fit's tolerance is 4.48 %. Nothing here touches it.

assumptions.name: estimator
assumptions.mine: For alpha: the sample variance of the framed positions. For the slope: an unweighted least squares over four velocities. Neither is the Lorentzian fit of r4, so r4's +0.8 to +1.2 % bias does not apply here -- but the question of which estimator each side uses is the same question and is still open.

worth.note: Unquantified for this route. The r4 figure is for the f_c route and is not transferable.

assumptions.note: Carried unresolved from r4 and r5.

gaps.what: A wall, and therefore h0 as a physical measurement.
gaps.why: BD has no hydrodynamic interactions, and k* carries no drag, so all six rungs are the same dimensionless run.
gaps.consequence: No simulation on this side will ever measure a wall factor it was not given. h0 as a physical quantity is not reachable here, in this round or any later one.
gaps.would_need: Nothing this side can build. On your side, a direct z datum -- which is what r1's own falsifier says to redesign around.

gaps.what: The per-rung scatter on the drag-slope gamma, on real data.
gaps.why: The 7.2-9.5 % here is measured on exact OU with your declared camera parameters, not on your instrument. P7's 2026-09-03 data is the only thing that can confirm it, and it is on the instrument PC.
gaps.consequence: The 1.8x-over-tolerance finding rests on a simulated per-rung error. sigma_gamma_max = 4.48 % does NOT -- it is a property of the fit and is the number to compare P7 against.

gaps.what: Whether the ladder's six heights are the right six.
gaps.why: r7 gaps[2] assigns this to bd and it is genuinely ours. Not done in this round, deliberately: it is an optimisation and the tolerance question had to be answered first, because a better ladder is only worth designing if the measurement can get inside the tolerance at all.
gaps.consequence: sigma_gamma_max = 4.48 % is for YOUR six heights. A different six would move it, plausibly upward, since the near rungs carry the most Faxen signal and currently get the least statistics (T_obs/tau_k = 201 at h = 3.0 against 323 at h = 10).
gaps.would_need: The same propagation, swept over ladder designs. Cheap -- seconds, not a run. Worth doing once P7 says what scatter is actually achievable.

gaps.why: Open since r4. This round uses a sample variance and an unweighted four-point slope, neither of which is r4's Lorentzian fit.
gaps.consequence: Central values are comparable between the two sides only to the extent the estimators match, and nobody has checked.

findings.what: Your claim is confirmed and it does not save the measurement.
findings.am_says: sigma_gamma_max is at or above 3 %, which is what our budget assumes.
findings.bd_says: 4.48 %, so yes, with room -- and at 3 % the fit returns h0 to 0.131 um, so r1's +/-0.195 um was conservative given its own assumption. The model was never the problem. The measured per-rung scatter is 7.2-9.5 %, which is 1.8x the tolerance, and the forward fit at that scatter gives 0.433-0.450 um.

findings.what: r1's own falsifier has fired, five rounds after it was written.
findings.am_says: r1: 'if its scatter exceeds ~0.4 um once finite T_obs, motion blur and localisation noise are included, then the ladder does not produce a trapping height and the run should be redesigned around a direct z datum instead.'
findings.bd_says: 0.433-0.450 um, measured with exactly those three included, stable across injected h0 of 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 um. The criterion was pre-registered in round one and this is the first round that could evaluate it.

findings.what: The per-rung error is the equipartition alpha, not the drag slope.
findings.am_says: (the budget carries one combined 3 % per rung)
findings.bd_says: Decomposed: sigma from alpha is 7.3-9.5 %, sigma from the slope is 1.3-1.6 %. The slope is not the problem and lengthening the drive segments buys little; the variance estimate is the problem, and it is bounded by T_obs/tau_k, which the plan sets to 201-323.

findings.what: A uniform bias on gamma lands on gamma_0, not on h0.
findings.bd_says: h0 is set by the SHAPE of gamma(h), so a multiplicative bias common to all rungs cancels out of it. Measured: the camera moves gamma_0 by -4.65 % and h0 by nothing resolvable (1.106 camera on against 1.136 off, at h0_true = 1.0, both +/-0.03). So the epsilon bias threatens gamma_bulk and not the trapping height -- which is the opposite of what r1 feared, and good news for the one quantity r1 cared about.

findings.what: The OU reduction was checked against the integrator, not assumed.
findings.bd_says: HOOMD Brownian at k* = 21221, dt/tau_k = 0.002, T_obs/tau_k = 322.9, N = 1000: the slope d<x>/dv against the analytic -1/k* is +0.032 %, <x> within -0.36 to +0.14 %, var within -1.31 to +0.03 %. That is a different KIND of evidence from the analytic layer, which is why it was run.
